title: DeLorean vs Cybertruck: Two Stainless Steel Bets

scenes.text: Two vehicles, forty years apart, both with unpainted stainless steel bodies and big promises. The DeLorean DMC-12 targeted twelve thousand dollars and launched at twenty-five thousand. The Tesla Cybertruck was shown at thirty-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety and launched at sixty thousand, nine hundred ninety. This video compares the two bets using published numbers, and shows where they are not comparable.
scenes.caption: DELOREAN vs CYBERTRUCK: TWO STAINLESS STEEL BETS

scenes.text: Our sources are Wikipedia pages on the DeLorean DMC-12, the Cybertruck, John DeLorean and the Texas DeLorean company, plus Business Insider, Yahoo Autos, InsideEVs and ThePricer. The pages sometimes disagree with each other, and the two vehicles were sold in very different eras. Our own arithmetic is labelled.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA (DMC-12 · CYBERTRUCK · JOHN DELOREAN · DMC TEXAS) · BUSINESS INSIDER · YAHOO AUTOS · INSIDEEVS · THEPRICER · OUR ARITHMETIC IS LABELLED · DIFFERENT ERAS, NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE

scenes.text: Start with the price promise. For the DeLorean, Wikipedia says the name DMC-12 came from a target price of twelve thousand dollars, and the production car launched in nineteen eighty-one at twenty-five thousand. By our arithmetic, that is a hundred and eight percent above the target. The car's final price in nineteen eighty-three was thirty-four thousand.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: '12' FROM A $12,000 TARGET · 1981 LAUNCH $25,000 = +108% · 1983 $34,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: For the Cybertruck, Wikipedia says the twenty nineteen reveal promised a base price of thirty-nine thousand, nine hundred dollars, targeted for late twenty twenty-one. At the delivery event on the thirtieth of November twenty twenty-three, Tesla priced the rear-drive at sixty thousand, nine hundred ninety, the all-wheel-drive at seventy-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety, and the Cyberbeast at ninety-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 2019 REVEAL — BASE $39,900 (LATE 2021 TARGET) · 30 NOV 2023 — RWD $60,990 · AWD $79,990 · CYBERBEAST $99,990

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the rear-drive price is fifty-three percent above the twenty nineteen base price. The Wikipedia page quotes a range of fifty-three to sixty-four percent for the increases, but we can only reproduce the fifty-three percent from our notes. The higher trims were not in the twenty nineteen price list we have, so a like-for-like comparison is not possible.
scenes.caption: $60,990 ÷ $39,900 = +52.9% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WIKIPEDIA RANGE 53–64% — UPPER END NOT REPRODUCIBLE FROM OUR NOTES

scenes.text: So both vehicles launched above the number first said out loud. The DeLorean overshoot was bigger in percentage terms, a hundred and eight percent against fifty-three. But the Cybertruck then changed again. In April twenty twenty-five, Wikipedia says, a Long Range model came at sixty-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety, nine thousand dollars above the original rear-drive price.
scenes.caption: DELOREAN +108% vs CYBERTRUCK RWD +53% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WIKIPEDIA: LONG RANGE (APR 2025) $69,990 = +$9,000 vs ORIGINAL $60,990 (+14.8%, OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Later, the price moved down. Wikipedia says that in February twenty twenty-six the all-wheel-drive was cut to fifty-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety, with delivery beginning in April twenty twenty-seven. By our arithmetic, that is twenty-five percent below the original seventy-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety. The page also says the Long Range was discontinued in September twenty twenty-five.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: AWD CUT TO $59,990 (FEB 2026), DELIVERY FROM APR 2027 · $59,990 ÷ $79,990 = −25.0% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · LONG RANGE DISCONTINUED SEPT 2025

scenes.text: Now time. The DeLorean's first prototype appeared in October nineteen seventy-six, according to Wikipedia, and production began in December nineteen eighty. By our arithmetic, that is four years and two months. The first production car was announced on the twenty-first of January nineteen eighty-one, in a factory at Dunmurry, near Belfast.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: PROTOTYPE 1 OCT 1976 → PRODUCTION DEC 1980 ≈ 4 YR 2 MO (OUR ARITHMETIC) · FIRST PRODUCTION CAR ANNOUNCED 21 JAN 1981 · DUNMURRY, NEAR BELFAST

scenes.text: The Cybertruck concept was unveiled on the twenty-first of November twenty nineteen. Customer deliveries began on the thirtieth of November twenty twenty-three. By our arithmetic, that is four years and nine days. Tesla had targeted production for late twenty twenty-one, so, by the same arithmetic, deliveries were about two years late.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: UNVEILED 21 NOV 2019 → DELIVERIES 30 NOV 2023 = 4 YEARS 9 DAYS · TARGET LATE 2021 → ~2 YEARS LATE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Wikipedia page adds the stages: first unit assembled at Gigafactory Texas in July twenty twenty-three, which Tesla later called pilot production, and a delivery event with final pricing and specifications. The reveal promised up to five hundred miles of range. The production truck was rated at three hundred forty, according to the same page.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: FIRST UNIT JULY 2023 (PILOT PRODUCTION) · 2019 PROMISE: UP TO 500 MI · PRODUCTION RATING: 340 MI → −32% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The DeLorean's promises changed too. Wikipedia lists a claimed zero to sixty of eight point eight seconds against a measured ten point five, and a claimed top speed of a hundred thirty against a hundred ten tested. So both vehicles had gaps between the first claim and the delivered figure, though the Cybertruck's gap was in range and the DeLorean's in speed.
scenes.caption: DELOREAN: 0–60 8.8 CLAIMED vs 10.5 MEASURED · TOP SPEED 130 vs 110 (WIKIPEDIA) · CYBERTRUCK: 500 MI PROMISED vs 340 RATED (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Business Insider's December twenty nineteen piece quotes Tesla's own claims for the then-unreleased truck: tri-motor trim, five hundred miles of range, zero to sixty in two point nine seconds, and towing over fourteen thousand pounds. Wikipedia later lists the Cyberbeast at two point six seconds, and towing of eleven thousand pounds for the all-wheel-drive. The numbers moved in both directions.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER (DEC 2019, TESLA CLAIMS): 500 MI · 0–60 2.9 S · TOWING >14,000 LB · WIKIPEDIA (PRODUCTION): CYBERBEAST 0–60 2.6 S · AWD TOWING 11,000 LB

scenes.text: Both vehicles are known for stainless steel, and Business Insider noted in December twenty nineteen that apart from a few one-off promotional cars, automakers have not used it for production vehicles. The DeLorean's body is brushed SAE three-oh-four stainless steel over a fibreglass underbody, per Wikipedia, and left unpainted. The chassis is a steel backbone derived from the Lotus Esprit.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER (DEC 2019): STAINLESS RARELY USED IN PRODUCTION CARS · WIKIPEDIA: DELOREAN = BRUSHED SAE 304 OVER FIBREGLASS UNDERBODY; STEEL BACKBONE CHASSIS FROM LOTUS ESPRIT

scenes.text: The Cybertruck is different in structure. Wikipedia says its stainless panels are three-hundred-series steel, one point eight millimetres on the doors and one point four on the body, which is zero point zero seven one and zero point zero five five inches. The panels are laser-cut and bent rather than stamped, using a method Tesla calls air bending.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 300-SERIES STAINLESS · DOORS 1.8 MM (0.071 IN) · BODY 1.4 MM (0.055 IN) · LASER-CUT AND BENT, NOT STAMPED ('AIR BENDING')

scenes.text: Business Insider reported that Tesla calls the material ultra-hard thirty-X cold-rolled stainless steel, which it says is superior to three-oh-four. The Wikipedia page we read does not mention thirty-X. That is a discrepancy between two sources for the same truck, and it is Tesla's own marketing name, not a measured result we can verify.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER (DEC 2019): TESLA CALLS IT 'ULTRA-HARD 30X COLD-ROLLED STAINLESS STEEL', 'SUPERIOR TO 304' · WIKIPEDIA PAGE DOES NOT MENTION '30X' · COMPANY MARKETING NAME, NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

scenes.text: The DeLorean's steel pitch was modest. Business Insider says it was that scratches could be buffed out, and called the shimmering skin mostly marketing. The Cybertruck's pitch, per InsideEVs, is that Tesla markets it as dent-proof, rust-proof and even bulletproof, which the article says are not exactly accurate. We are quoting those as claims and critiques, not testing them.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER: DELOREAN PITCH — SCRATCHES CAN BE BUFFED OUT; 'MOSTLY MARKETING' · INSIDEEVS (21 DEC 2024): TESLA MARKETS CYBERTRUCK AS DENT-PROOF, RUST-PROOF, BULLETPROOF — 'NOT EXACTLY ACCURATE' (ARTICLE'S VIEW)

scenes.text: Owners reported problems. Business Insider, republished on Yahoo Autos in March twenty twenty-four, said fingerprints were the most common complaint, along with orange specks. Tesla engineer Wes Morrill said on X that the specks were surface contamination from the factory or rail transport, not rust, and that they could be cleaned off easily. Elon Musk replied yeah.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER / YAHOO AUTOS (10 MAR 2024): FINGERPRINTS = MOST COMMON COMPLAINT · WES MORRILL (TESLA ENGINEER, ON X): ORANGE SPECKS = SURFACE CONTAMINATION, NOT RUSTING METAL · MUSK REPLIED 'YEAH'

scenes.text: The fixes cost money. The same article says four of six owners had wrapped their trucks or were in the process, and wraps cost upwards of five thousand dollars. One owner chose a clear protection film of about five thousand to prevent fingerprints. Barkeepers Friend was the most recommended cleaner. We have no equivalent cost record for DeLorean owners in these sources.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER / YAHOO: 4 OF 6 OWNERS WRAPPED OR WRAPPING · WRAPS 'UPWARDS OF $5,000' · CLEAR PPF ≈ $5,000 · BARKEEPERS FRIEND MOST RECOMMENDED · DELOREAN EQUIVALENT: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: A repair example. InsideEVs, in December twenty twenty-four, reported that a Tesla collision centre quoted three thousand dollars to fix a dented Cybertruck door, with eight hundred twenty-eight of it for a new door panel. The owner fixed the dent with a friend for about twenty-five dollars, using a suction cup on a warmed panel. It is one owner's experience, as the article notes.
scenes.caption: INSIDEEVS (21 DEC 2024): TESLA QUOTE $3,000 ($828 DOOR PANEL) · OWNER FIX ≈ $25 · ONE OWNER, ONE DENT · $3,000 ÷ $25 = 120× (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Power and speed show the biggest gap. The DeLorean's V6 made one hundred thirty horsepower, and Business Insider quotes ten point five seconds to sixty. Wikipedia lists the Cybertruck at three hundred fifteen horsepower for the Long Range, six hundred for the all-wheel-drive, and eight hundred forty-five for the Cyberbeast, with zero-to-sixty times of six point two, four point one and two point six seconds.
scenes.caption: DELOREAN 130 HP · 10.5 S · CYBERTRUCK LONG RANGE 315 HP / 6.2 S · AWD 600 HP / 4.1 S · CYBERBEAST 845 HP / 2.6 S (WIKIPEDIA; BUSINESS INSIDER)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Cyberbeast has six and a half times the DeLorean's horsepower and gets to sixty in a quarter of the time. Even the slowest Cybertruck, the Long Range at six point two seconds, is forty-one percent quicker than the DeLorean's ten point five. Of course, forty years of progress separate them, so this is a measure of eras.
scenes.caption: 845 ÷ 130 = 6.5× · 2.6 ÷ 10.5 = 24.8% OF THE TIME · 6.2 vs 10.5 S = −41.0% (OUR ARITHMETIC; 1981 vs 2023)

scenes.text: Size and weight. The Cybertruck is two hundred twenty-three point seven inches long, nearly eighty inches wide and seventy point seven tall, per Wikipedia, and weighs sixty-six hundred sixty pounds in all-wheel-drive form. The DeLorean's page lists a thirty-five foot turning circle and brake sizes, but no weight or length in our copy, so a size comparison is impossible from our sources.
scenes.caption: CYBERTRUCK: 223.74 IN L · 79.99 IN W · 70.7 IN H · AWD 6,660 LB (WIKIPEDIA) · DELOREAN: LENGTH / WEIGHT NOT IN OUR COPY → NO SIZE COMPARISON

scenes.text: Battery weight alone is notable. Wikipedia lists the Cybertruck's pack at fifteen hundred ninety pounds. By our arithmetic, that is twenty-four percent of the truck's sixty-six hundred sixty pounds. The pack stores one hundred twenty-three kilowatt-hours and can charge at up to three hundred fifty kilowatts, according to the same page.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: PACK 1,590 LB · 123 KWH · UP TO 350 KW CHARGING · 1,590 ÷ 6,660 = 23.9% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Range and towing vary by trim. Wikipedia lists EPA range of three hundred thirty-one to three hundred sixty-two miles for the Long Range, three hundred fourteen to three hundred forty for all-wheel-drive, and three hundred one to three hundred twenty for the Cyberbeast. Towing is seventy-five hundred pounds for the Long Range and eleven thousand for all-wheel-drive. The DeLorean was not designed to tow, says Business Insider.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: LONG RANGE 331–362 MI / 7,500 LB TOW · AWD 314–340 MI / 11,000 LB · CYBERBEAST 301–320 MI · BUSINESS INSIDER: DELOREAN 'NOT MEANT TO TOW'

scenes.text: Now what actually sold. Wikipedia estimates eighty-nine hundred seventy-five DeLoreans were built across three model years. About three thousand had been sold by the end of nineteen eighty-one, against seventy-five hundred built. By our arithmetic, a forty percent sell-through. The company was in receivership by February nineteen eighty-two.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 8,975 BUILT (1981–83 BY VIN) · END-1981: ~7,500 BUILT vs ~3,000 SOLD = 40% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · RECEIVERSHIP FEB 1982

scenes.text: The Cybertruck sold eleven thousand, six hundred eighty-eight by June twenty twenty-four, and thirty-eight thousand, nine hundred sixty-five in all of twenty twenty-four, per Kelley Blue Book as cited on Wikipedia. By our arithmetic, that single year is four and a third times the total DeLorean production. It was the best-selling electric pickup in the United States that year.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 11,688 BY JUNE 2024 · 38,965 IN 2024 (KBB) → 4.34× 8,975 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · BEST-SELLING US EV PICKUP IN 2024

scenes.text: But the trend turned. Wikipedia says just over sixteen thousand were sold in the first three quarters of twenty twenty-five. Forbes reported sales were about ten percent of production capacity in April twenty twenty-five. The page also says forty-six thousand, ninety-six vehicles had been produced before the twenty-seventh of February twenty twenty-five, per a recall filing.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: ~16,000+ SOLD IN FIRST 3 QUARTERS OF 2025 · FORBES (APR 2025): SALES ≈ 10% OF PRODUCTION CAPACITY · 46,096 PRODUCED BEFORE 27 FEB 2025 (RECALL FIGURE)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, sixteen thousand in three quarters averages about five thousand three hundred a quarter, down from about ten thousand a quarter in twenty twenty-four. That is a fall of roughly forty-five percent, based on rounded numbers. And the Foundation Series, capped at twenty-five thousand and sold at a twenty thousand dollar premium, ended in January twenty twenty-five.
scenes.caption: 16,000 ÷ 3 ≈ 5,333/QUARTER vs 38,965 ÷ 4 ≈ 9,741/QUARTER → −45% (OUR ARITHMETIC; ROUNDED) · FOUNDATION SERIES: +$20,000, CAP 25,000, ENDED JAN 2025 (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Then the preorders. Wikipedia says Elon Musk claimed two hundred fifty thousand preorders in the five days after the twenty nineteen unveiling, with a refundable hundred-dollar deposit, later raised to two hundred fifty. By our arithmetic, forty-six thousand produced is eighteen percent of two hundred fifty thousand, though deposits and sales are different things.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 250,000 PREORDERS IN 5 DAYS (MUSK'S CLAIM) · $100 REFUNDABLE DEPOSIT → $250 AFTER 30 NOV 2023 · 46,096 ÷ 250,000 = 18.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC; DEPOSITS ≠ SALES)

scenes.text: The DeLorean's distribution was different. Wikipedia says that in March nineteen eighty-two telegrams asked all three hundred forty-three dealers to buy six cars each, and none responded with an order. By our arithmetic, that is a request for two thousand fifty-eight cars. It is a sign of how unsold the nineteen eighty-two stock was.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MARCH 1982 — 343 DEALERS ASKED TO BUY 6 CARS EACH · NO ORDERS · 343 × 6 = 2,058 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Quality issues sit on both sides. Wikipedia says early DeLoreans needed up to two hundred hours of work at quality centres, and four recalls were issued. For the Cybertruck, the same site lists recalls for the accelerator pedal in April twenty twenty-four, the wiper in June, a trim panel in March twenty twenty-five, and wheel-rotor nuts in May twenty twenty-six.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: DELOREAN — UP TO 200 HOURS OF QUALITY-CENTRE WORK · 4 RECALLS · CYBERTRUCK — PEDAL (16 APR 2024) · WIPER (18 JUN 2024) · TRIM PANEL (20 MAR 2025) · WHEEL-ROTOR NUTS (8 MAY 2026, 173 RWD TRUCKS)

scenes.text: The page says ten recalls as of October twenty twenty-five, but its table lists eleven including May twenty twenty-six. That is a discrepancy inside the source. By our arithmetic, ten or eleven recalls over about two and a half years of deliveries is four to five a year, against four DeLorean recalls over about two years of production.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA TEXT: 10 RECALLS (OCT 2025) vs TABLE: 11 (INCL. MAY 2026) · 10–11 ÷ ~2.4 YEARS ≈ 4–5/YEAR vs DELOREAN 4 IN ~2 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC; COUNTS NOT NORMALISED BY VOLUME)

scenes.text: The recalls differ in scale. A recall counts every vehicle affected, and the Cybertruck's numbers are larger because far more were sold. The sources we read give vehicle counts for only one Cybertruck recall, 173 rear-drive trucks for the May twenty twenty-six wheel-rotor nut issue. We have no counts for the DeLorean recalls.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MAY 2026 RECALL = 173 RWD TRUCKS · OTHER CYBERTRUCK RECALL COUNTS AND DELOREAN RECALL COUNTS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: A design thread connects them. Wikipedia says Giorgetto Giugiaro, who designed the DeLorean, is credited with the origami design trend, and that he said in twenty twenty-three the Cybertruck would find admirers. Elon Musk, it adds, cited Blade Runner and Wet Nellie, the Lotus Esprit from The Spy Who Loved Me, as inspirations. Giugiaro also designed that Esprit.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: GIUGIARO (DELOREAN, LOTUS ESPRIT, BMW M1) SAID IN 2023 THE CYBERTRUCK WOULD FIND ADMIRERS · MUSK CITED BLADE RUNNER AND 'WET NELLIE' (LOTUS ESPRIT, THE SPY WHO LOVED ME) · GIUGIARO DESIGNED THE ESPRIT (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Other designers disagreed. Wikipedia quotes Frank Stephenson calling the Cybertruck almost repulsive but saying it has the potential to be extremely beautiful, and Adrian Clarke calling it a low polygon joke. Those are opinions. The Cybertruck's design chief is Franz von Holzhausen, Business Insider says, with some input from Elon Musk.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: FRANK STEPHENSON — 'ALMOST REPULSIVE… POTENTIAL TO BE EXTREMELY BEAUTIFUL' · ADRIAN CLARKE — 'LOW POLYGON JOKE' (OPINIONS) · BUSINESS INSIDER: DESIGNED BY FRANZ VON HOLZHAUSEN WITH INPUT FROM MUSK

scenes.text: Business Insider, in December twenty nineteen, called John DeLorean the most flamboyant personality in the car business of his day, and described Elon Musk as something of the John DeLorean of this era, though it says Musk had far exceeded DeLorean's achievements. That is the writer's comparison in twenty nineteen, not a fact we can test.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER (DEC 2019): DELOREAN = 'MOST FLAMBOYANT PERSONALITY IN THE CAR BUSINESS OF HIS DAY' · MUSK = 'SOMETHING OF THE JOHN DELOREAN OF THIS ERA' BUT FAR EXCEEDING HIS ACHIEVEMENTS (WRITER'S OPINION)

scenes.text: There is a big difference in what happened to the companies. Wikipedia says the DeLorean company filed for bankruptcy on the twenty-sixth of October nineteen eighty-two, days after John DeLorean's arrest on the nineteenth. Tesla is not in that position in any of our sources, and we do not speculate. The comparison is of two products, not two balance sheets.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: DELOREAN ARRESTED 19–20 OCT 1982 · DMC BANKRUPT 26 OCT 1982 · TESLA'S FINANCIAL POSITION: NOT IN OUR SOURCES → NO BALANCE-SHEET COMPARISON

scenes.text: Resale. ThePricer says a standard DeLorean now costs roughly fifty to seventy-five thousand dollars in twenty twenty-six, with a manual premium of about ten percent. By our arithmetic, that is two to three times the original twenty-five thousand, unadjusted. Wikipedia adds that the original price equals about eighty-nine thousand dollars in twenty twenty-five money, so a used DeLorean sells below that.
scenes.caption: THEPRICER (2026): $50,000–$75,000 · WIKIPEDIA: $25,000 (1981) ≈ $89,000 IN 2025 DOLLARS → $50–75K = 56%–84% OF THAT (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Cybertruck's secondhand prices are not in our sources, so we cannot compare the two on resale. What we do have are new-price changes: from sixty thousand, nine hundred ninety to fifty-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety on the all-wheel-drive at one point. We will not invent a depreciation figure. A later video can revisit this when sources exist.
scenes.caption: CYBERTRUCK USED PRICES / DEPRECIATION: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · NEW PRICE: AWD $79,990 → $59,990 (FEB 2026, WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Prices from different eras need adjusting. Wikipedia converts the DeLorean's nineteen eighty-one price of twenty-five thousand dollars to about eighty-nine thousand in twenty twenty-five dollars. By our arithmetic, that is forty-six percent more than the Cybertruck's rear-drive launch price of sixty thousand, nine hundred ninety, and eleven percent more than the all-wheel-drive at seventy-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: $25,000 (1981) ≈ $89,000 (2025) · $89,000 ÷ $60,990 = 1.46× · ÷ $79,990 = 1.11× (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT YEARS, TRIMS, EQUIPMENT)

scenes.text: The Cyberbeast at ninety-nine thousand, nine hundred ninety is about twelve percent above that inflation-adjusted DeLorean price, by our arithmetic. So in real terms, the DeLorean sat between the Cybertruck's all-wheel-drive and its top trim. That is a surprising place for a car with one hundred thirty horsepower and a measured zero to sixty of ten point five seconds.
scenes.caption: $99,990 ÷ $89,000 = +12.3% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · DELOREAN 130 HP / 10.5 S vs CYBERBEAST 845 HP / 2.6 S (WIKIPEDIA; BUSINESS INSIDER)

scenes.text: Business Insider, in twenty nineteen, noted a different contrast: the DeLorean cost twenty-five thousand dollars and could not drive itself, while Tesla's top-spec Cybertruck was about seventy thousand plus seven thousand for full self-driving. Those were Tesla's announced figures at the time, not final prices, and the production prices were later set differently.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER (DEC 2019): DELOREAN $25,000, 'COULD NOT DRIVE ITSELF' · CYBERTRUCK TOP SPEC ~$70,000 + $7,000 FSD (TESLA'S THEN-ANNOUNCED FIGURES) · PRODUCTION PRICES LATER DIFFERED (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: The Foundation Series shows the same habit of premium editions. Wikipedia says it carried a twenty thousand dollar premium and was capped at twenty-five thousand units. The DeLorean's equivalent was the gold-plated American Express car at eighty-five thousand dollars, planned for a hundred and sold twice. By our arithmetic, the Foundation cap was two hundred fifty times larger.
scenes.caption: CYBERTRUCK FOUNDATION SERIES: +$20,000, CAP 25,000 · DELOREAN GOLD CAR: $85,000, PLANNED 100, SOLD 2 (WIKIPEDIA) · 25,000 ÷ 100 = 250× (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Top speed is one place they overlap. Wikipedia lists a hundred twelve miles per hour for the Long Range Cybertruck and a hundred thirty for the all-wheel-drive, though its table places the hundred thirty under the Cyberbeast and the text under the all-wheel-drive. The DeLorean was claimed at a hundred thirty and tested at a hundred ten.
scenes.caption: CYBERTRUCK: 112 MPH (LONG RANGE) · 130 MPH (AWD PER TEXT; CYBERBEAST PER TABLE — CONFLICT) · DELOREAN: 130 CLAIMED, 110 TESTED (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the slowest Cybertruck's hundred twelve is two percent above the DeLorean's tested hundred ten. After forty years, top speed barely moved for the base truck, while acceleration improved massively. That is partly because the Cybertruck is a work-oriented pickup with a rated tow capacity, and the DeLorean was a sports-car-shaped coupe that could not tow.
scenes.caption: 112 vs 110 MPH = +1.8% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · CYBERTRUCK LONG RANGE TOW 7,500 LB (WIKIPEDIA) · DELOREAN 'NOT MEANT TO TOW' (BUSINESS INSIDER)

scenes.text: Charging is something the DeLorean never needed. Wikipedia says the Cybertruck can add one hundred twenty-eight or one hundred thirty-six miles in fifteen minutes at four hundred volts, and charge at up to three hundred fifty kilowatts at eight hundred. By our arithmetic, one hundred thirty-six miles in fifteen minutes is about five hundred forty miles of range per hour of charging.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: +128 / +136 MI IN 15 MIN AT 400 V · UP TO 350 KW AT 800 V · 136 MI × 4 = 544 MI PER HOUR (OUR ARITHMETIC; BEST-CASE FIGURE)

scenes.text: Showmanship connects them. At the twenty nineteen reveal, Wikipedia says two Armor Glass windows shattered when metal balls were thrown at them, and Musk later blamed an earlier sledgehammer strike. For the DeLorean, the showmanship was the gold car, the celebrity circuit, and the show car at the National Automobile Dealers show in nineteen eighty.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: CYBERTRUCK REVEAL 21 NOV 2019 — TWO 'ARMOR GLASS' WINDOWS SHATTERED; MUSK LATER BLAMED AN EARLIER SLEDGEHAMMER STRIKE · DELOREAN: NADA SHOW CAR 1980 (VISIONEERING), GOLD CAR PROMOTION

scenes.text: A drag race is a further example. Wikipedia says Musk described a race as a quarter mile, but footage analysis suggested an eighth of a mile. We report that as a disputed point on the page, not a conclusion of ours. It shows that performance claims, for Tesla as for DeLorean, were checked against evidence afterwards.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MUSK SAID THE DRAG RACE WAS A QUARTER-MILE; FOOTAGE ANALYSIS SUGGESTED AN EIGHTH · DISPUTED POINT, NOT RESOLVED IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: One more difference is the supply chain. Business Insider, in twenty nineteen, argued that because no automaker builds cars from stainless steel today, there is no meaningful supply chain for it. For the DeLorean, the factory in Northern Ireland had funding of about a hundred million pounds, according to John DeLorean's Wikipedia page. The Cybertruck's funding is not in our sources.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER (DEC 2019): NO MEANINGFUL STAINLESS SUPPLY CHAIN IN CARS · WIKIPEDIA: DELOREAN FACTORY ~£100 MILLION INCENTIVES · CYBERTRUCK FUNDING: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: There is also the workforce. John DeLorean's page says the Dunmurry plant employed over two thousand workers at its peak, and produced around nine thousand cars. By our arithmetic, that is about four and a half cars per worker over the car's life, which is not a productivity figure, since the workforce changed over time and our sources give no yearly staffing.
scenes.caption: 2,000+ WORKERS AT PEAK · ~9,000 CARS → ~4.5 CARS PER PEAK WORKER (OUR ARITHMETIC; NOT A PRODUCTIVITY FIGURE; STAFFING BY YEAR NOT IN OUR SOURCES)

scenes.text: And the rights to the name. The Texas DeLorean company, per Wikipedia, has no direct connection with the original firm and has faced lawsuits, including an Italdesign judgment of four point six million dollars in early twenty twenty-six. Tesla's trademark and design position is not covered in our sources. This is a story about two vehicles, and the DeLorean has an unusually messy afterlife.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (DMC TEXAS): NO DIRECT CONNECTION TO ORIGINAL COMPANY · ITALDESIGN JUDGMENT $4.6 M (EARLY 2026) · TESLA'S TRADEMARK / DESIGN POSITION: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: So which bet was better? On sales, the Cybertruck, with thirty-eight thousand in a year against a lifetime total of about nine thousand for the DeLorean. On time to market, they were similar, four years or so each. On price overshoot, the DeLorean was worse. On steel, both had issues, but the Cybertruck is a structural exoskeleton and the DeLorean a skin.
scenes.caption: SALES: CYBERTRUCK 38,965 (2024) vs DELOREAN ~8,975 LIFETIME · TIME: ~4 YEARS EACH · PRICE OVERSHOOT: +108% vs +53% · STEEL: STRUCTURAL PANELS vs SKIN (OUR SUMMARY OF CITED FIGURES)
scenes.chapter: So which was the better bet?

scenes.text: The honest answer is that they were bets in different times. The DeLorean was a small company with a government-backed factory, and its sales collapsed within two years. The Cybertruck came from a large manufacturer, and its sales were strong in year one and weaker later. Our sources do not allow a final verdict on the second.
scenes.caption: DELOREAN: COLLAPSE WITHIN ~2 YEARS OF LAUNCH (WIKIPEDIA) · CYBERTRUCK: STRONG 2024, WEAKER 2025 (WIKIPEDIA/FORBES) · FINAL VERDICT ON CYBERTRUCK: NOT SUPPORTED BY OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: What is missing. The DeLorean's weight and length. The Cybertruck's used prices. Dealer data for both. A consistent recall count for the Cybertruck. A test comparing both bodies for corrosion or dents under identical conditions. If you have a documented number, share it in the comments and we will update the description.
